name: Meadow Bud Cluster

yarn.description: Cotton or cotton-blend yarn for tiny buds

gauge: Gauge is not critical because the buds are small decorative elements. Use a firm tension so the stuffing does not show.

steps.label: Rnd 3
steps.text: Sc in each st around. Lightly stuff the bud before the next rnd.

steps.label: Rnd 5
steps.text: Sc in each st around. Fasten off, leaving a 15-centimetre sewing tail.

assembly: Cut one 12-centimetre wire for the central stem and six 8-centimetre wires for side branches.
Place a wire tip against the underside of each bud. Use its sewing tail to make three tight passes through the six final-rnd stitches and around the wire, securing one bud to each wire.
Position the bud on the 12-centimetre wire at the top. On the six shorter wires, leave the bud at one end and use the unbudded end for joining.

Twist the unbudded end of two side branches around the central stem 2 centimetres above its lower end. Attach two more branches 3.5 centimetres above the lower end and the final pair 5 centimetres above it.
Arrange each pair on opposite sides of the central stem. Bend the branches gently upward so their buds form an airy, tapered cluster below the central bud.
Stretch-wrap floral tape from beneath each bud down its branch wire. Continue the tape over the branch joins and down the central stem, overlapping the tape slightly.
finishing: Fasten off each bud after Rnd 5, leaving the stated sewing tail for attaching it to its wire.
Weave the remaining yarn tails into the underside of their buds after the buds have been secured to the wires.
Bend the lower end of the central wire back by 5 millimetres and cover it with floral tape so no sharp wire is exposed.
Gently adjust the wired branches to create an open, balanced spray before attaching it to wall-hoop décor.
notes: Keep the buds lightly stuffed; overstuffing makes the small rounds stretch and show the yarn stuffing.
For a longer or fuller filler, make extra buds and add them as additional wired side branches.
